title: FMRB executive order signs with a parallel House joint resolution by end-Q2 2026
body: By end-Q2 2026 the Frontier Model Review Board executive order is signed and a parallel House joint resolution on the same 30-day technical-review track clears subcommittee markup, landing the United States' frontier-AI oversight instrument as a coupled executive-and-legislative pair rather than the executive order alone. The Tuesday catalysts are concrete and converge on a clearing-procedure sequence on both branches at once. A Tuesday Lawfare procedural note reports the classified-annex response clock advancing to its fourth calendar day with the deadline now at T-minus-two business days to the Friday May 22 expiry, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Director's office filing the second substantive submission against the Senate Cyber Subcommittee's classified-annex follow-up question set on top of Monday's first submission from NIST Director Locascio's office, and the remaining six witnesses confirming response drafts will land inside the deadline window. A Tuesday Just Security analysis restates that the classified-annex question set is the last remaining open procedural gate, observes that two of eight witnesses on record inside the first two business days is on the steeper response cadence the eight-witness slate had targeted, and confirms White House Office of Science and Technology Policy holding the line that the order remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology converted Monday's markup-scheduling decision into a calendar entry for the parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft, with the markup notice posted Tuesday morning per a PYMNTS Capitol-Hill note as the first formal House-track movement on the Frontier Model Review Board track since the order's signing window opened. The Tuesday CSO Online note on the CISA federal-civilian operational directive — now into its first full operating day with the Friday May 22 compliance window keyed to the same eleven-CVE Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy the executive order's technical review will lean on — establishes an executive-branch operational instrument the order can cite when signed. The structural force is that once the eight-witness classified-annex response slate is on a steeper cadence than the deadline requires with two responses already on record, OSTP has fixed no signing window before May 22 while leaving the post-May-22 window open, the House parallel-track joint resolution has a posted subcommittee markup notice on the same 30-day technical-review shape, and CISA has already published a federal-civilian operational directive on the same agent-loader taxonomy the executive order will reference, the order's signing compresses to clearing-procedure arithmetic — classified-annex close plus interagency-review close plus the post-deadline signing window lands the executive order signed inside Q2 2026 with the House subcommittee markup landing the parallel joint resolution inside the same quarter. The most likely landing is the Frontier Model Review Board executive order signing in the last week of May or first half of June 2026, the parallel House Energy and Commerce joint resolution clearing subcommittee markup inside Q2 2026, the CISA federal-civilian operational directive cited as the operational precedent inside the order's preamble, and the order plus the joint resolution landing as a coupled executive-and-legislative pair rather than an executive instrument standing alone. Bear case is a procedural slip from one or two of the remaining six classified-annex respondents pushing the signing window into early Q3 2026 with the House markup following inside the same window; absent that slip, end-Q2 2026 lands the Frontier Model Review Board executive order signed alongside a parallel House joint resolution clearing subcommittee markup.

reasoning.because: Two of eight classified-annex responses are on record by day four; the May 22 deadline sits at T-2.
reasoning.given: OSTP fixed no signing before May 22; the House posted a parallel markup; CISA shipped a directive.
reasoning.so_that: The FMRB executive order signs while a parallel House joint resolution clears subcommittee markup.
reasoning.landing: By end-Q2 2026; coupled executive-and-legislative US frontier-AI instrument.
reasoning.plain_language: The US AI oversight order is on track to be signed within weeks, and the House is moving its own matching bill at the same time.

summary: Two of eight classified-annex responses are on record by day four, the May 22 deadline sits at T-2 days, and the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee posted a parallel-track markup notice. By end-Q2 2026 the FMRB executive order signs alongside a parallel House joint resolution clearing markup.
